item.title: Correction · Waterfront Park: The City's Legistar pages for the amended development agreement…
item.description: The City's Legistar pages for the amended development agreement (File 260724) and its zoning ordinance (File 260770) list both as passed and enacted on October 13, 2026 (Mayor approved; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26). This record had said enactment was not confirmed. The final text and the date the ordinances take effect were not read, so the record's height and use figures still show the adopted limits. Source: SF Board of Supervisors, Legistar, BOS File 260724 and File 260770 (https://sfgov.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=8127453&GUID=CC4AC1DD-BF51-4585-86E8-0A5D44AA3745).

item.title: Correction · Waterfront Park: The Waterfront Park page now describes its shape as what is left of…

item.title: Correction · Waterfront Park: The 2031 expected completion was removed: it came from a 2020 press…
item.description: The 2031 expected completion was removed: it came from a 2020 press forecast of Phase 2's window that has not held, and the Port Commission's November 2025 memo says open space is tied to vertical development expected over the next 10-15 years; the timeline now cites that memo instead. The summary now says about 2 acres of the project's open space is on Port shoreline property under the $1-a-year lease, not that the park is largely on Port land. The Prequel Park note no longer says construction is underway (the Port memo says the developer hoped to start in the third quarter of 2026 and no source confirms a start), the 'and hotel' wording was dropped, the BCDC reviewing-agency claim was reworded to the scoping comment the Draft EIR records, the dead 2019 draft link was replaced with the final February 2020 document, and the land-use figure is tagged as a document rather than a rendering. An earlier change entry about the site-wide street contract was re-cited to the Port memo and the 2024 annual report. Source: Port of San Francisco, Port Commission Item 10A memo, 2025-11-14 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-11/111825_10a_potrero_power_station_lease_amendment_0.pdf); California Barrel Company, 2024 Annual Compliance Report, 2025-03-28 (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station); SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Draft EIR, Volume 1, 2018-10 (https://sfmea.sfplanning.org/2017-011878ENV_DEIR_Volume_1.pdf); SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final, 2020-02-26 (https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf).
item.source: Port of San Francisco, Port Commission Item 10A memo, 2025-11-14 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-11/111825_10a_potrero_power_station_lease_amendment_0.pdf); California Barrel Company, 2024 Annual Compliance Report, 2025-03-28 (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station); SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Draft EIR, Volume 1, 2018-10 (https://sfmea.sfplanning.org/2017-011878ENV_DEIR_Volume_1.pdf); SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final, 2020-02-26 (https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf)

item.title: Correction · Waterfront Park: Both of this record's cost entries turned out not to be…
item.description: Both of this record's cost entries turned out not to be park-specific: the $1/year Port Lease L-16662 rent covers the Port-owned shoreline premises shared with Prequel Park's Port sub-area (same lease, same source, same date as that record's own $1 entry), and the DeSilva Gates $39M Phase 1 Street Improvement contract is, per the 2024 annual compliance report, for utilities and infrastructure throughout the Phase 1 project area rather than for the park alone. Both were moved to the shared site-wide cost list (as a land/lease cost and an infrastructure cost), with this record pointing to each. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-11/111825_10a_potrero_power_station_lease_amendment_0.pdf; https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station.
item.source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-11/111825_10a_potrero_power_station_lease_amendment_0.pdf; https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station

item.title: Milestone · Waterfront Park: Demolition, rough grading and shoreline improvements by… (May 2023)
item.description: Demolition, rough grading and shoreline improvements by DeSilva Gates substantially complete: the 2023 annual report (letter of Nov 22, 2024) says DGC 'substantially completed the Horizontal Construction Project, which includes demolition, rough grading, and shoreline improvements, between July 2021 and May 2023' and that 'In May 2023, CBC wrapped up the first phase of the Project's shoreline improvements, which included deep soil mixing (DSM), approximately 800 linear feet of seawall construction, installation of steel pipe piles for the future dock, riprap slope protection, and the storm drain outfall'; the 2024 annual report (Mar 2025) says the demolition, excavation, abatement, pile driving and deep soil mixing work 'was substantially complete in May 2023', yet still lists the Horizontal Construction Project among contracts underway at December 2024 and says no Phase 1 horizontal infrastructure is complete. The seawall and shoreline work runs along the Bay frontage where the waterfront open spaces are planned; the reports do not say which parts lie within Waterfront Park, The Point or the Prequel Park band, and the Phase 1 application describes early work as 'geotechnical improvements along the shoreline and in areas of fill'. None of this is landscape construction of the park itself (May 2023). Source: California Barrel Company LLC (developer's compliance report, posted by SF Planning, M-Files), 2024-11-22; California Barrel Company LLC (developer's compliance report, posted by SF Planning, M-Files), 2025-03; California Barrel Company / SF Planning (M-Files: 'Potrero Power Station Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment Applications'), 2020-10.
item.source: California Barrel Company LLC (developer's compliance report, posted by SF Planning, M-Files), 2024-11-22; California Barrel Company LLC (developer's compliance report, posted by SF Planning, M-Files), 2025-03; California Barrel Company / SF Planning (M-Files: 'Potrero Power Station Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment Applications'), 2020-10
